name: 20-minute Asian
summary: Weeknight Asian dinners on the table in 20 minutes or less: Thai basil chicken, miso-ginger broiled salmon, a pho-style beef noodle soup, green curry with shrimp and kimchi fried rice. Real flavour, with the micronutrients covered.
howItWorks:
**Twenty minutes, counted honestly.** Every meal from Monday to Friday is 20 minutes or less of chopping, boiling the kettle, preheating the broiler and cooking. Monday to Friday dinners make two portions, and the second is the next day's lunch at zero minutes. Breakfasts take 7 to 13 minutes.

**The shortcuts.** Ready-cooked brown rice pouches, frozen edamame, bagged slaw mix, thin-sliced beef, quick-soak rice noodles and curry paste do the slow work. Thin cuts and a hot pan keep the cooking short. Every chicken and fish recipe has a thermometer check, and all produce, ginger and limes too, is washed before cutting.

**Fish and vitamin D.** Miso-ginger salmon on Tuesday and Atlantic mackerel on Friday carry the **omega-3**. Both fish bring some vitamin D, which is hard to get from food alone. Health Canada advises adults over 50 to take 400 IU of vitamin D a day.

**Salt and rice.** Reduced-sodium soy sauce, plus small measured amounts of miso, fish sauce and curry paste, keep sodium in check. Cooked rice always cools within 1 hour and is reheated only once, to 74 °C. An opened pouch, and the rice chilled on Friday night for Saturday's fried rice, keep 1 day.

**Sizes.** Light (1600 to 1800) trims the rice, noodles, oats, bread, coconut milk and oil and drops one snack on weekdays. The fish, meat, shrimp and eggs stay full size. Standard covers 1800 to 2400. Big (2400 to 3200) grows the portions: use your biggest wok, or two pans side by side, so the times hold. Two batches add about 5 minutes.

recipes.name: Korean-style egg and cabbage toast with gochujang honey
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Korean gilgeori toast, the street-stall egg sandwich, with a gochujang and honey spread instead of a sugary sauce
recipes.about: A thick, golden omelette studded with shredded cabbage, carrot and scallion, tucked between toasted multigrain bread with a sweet and gently spicy gochujang spread. It is on the table in about 13 minutes, and the eggs bring **protein and choline** to start the day.

ingredients.note: finely shredded, or from a bag of slaw mix
grated, or from the slaw mix

steps: Wash the cabbage, carrot and scallion before you cut them. Skip the rinse if your slaw bag says it is washed and ready to eat. Shred the cabbage, grate the carrot and slice the scallion.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper and wash your hands, then stir in the cabbage, carrot and scallion. Stir the gochujang and honey together in a small bowl. Pop the bread in the toaster.

Warm the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Pour in the egg mixture and push it into a square about the size of the bread. Cook about 3 minutes, until the underside is golden and the top is mostly set.
Flip it, press down gently and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, until the egg is completely set with no runny yolk or wet patches.
Spread the toast with the gochujang honey, fold or cut the omelette to fit, sandwich it and eat it warm.
recipes.tip: For a milder toast, use half the gochujang.

recipes.name: Yogurt bowl with banana, honey and toasted oat and sunflower crunch
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Asian yogurt and fruit cups, with a warm toasted oat and sunflower seed topping
recipes.about: Thick, tangy yogurt with sliced banana, a warm, crunchy topping of toasted oats, sunflower seeds and walnuts, and a drizzle of honey. It is ready in 7 minutes and gives you **protein, calcium and fibre**, with sunflower seeds for vitamin E and a little omega-3 from the walnuts.
steps: Peel and slice the banana.

Toast the oats, sunflower seeds and walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for about 3 minutes, stirring often, until they smell nutty and the oats turn light gold. Tip them onto a plate to cool for a minute.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and arrange the banana on top.
Scatter the warm crunch over the top and drizzle with the honey.
recipes.tip: Swap in mango or pineapple when you have it. Skip the honey for babies under 1.

recipes.name: Warm soy milk oats with tangerine and walnuts
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by the warm soy milk breakfasts of Taiwan and China, made into a creamy oat porridge
recipes.about: Rolled oats simmered in calcium-fortified soy milk until creamy, with juicy tangerine segments, crushed walnuts and a drizzle of honey. It is ready in 9 minutes and brings **fibre, plant protein and some omega-3** from the walnuts.
steps: Put the oats, soy milk, cinnamon and salt in a small pot and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring.
Cook 4 to 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the oats are thick and creamy.
Meanwhile, wash the tangerine, peel it, pull it into segments and chop the walnuts.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the tangerine, walnuts and honey.
recipes.tip: Shake the carton before you pour: the calcium in fortified soy milk settles at the bottom.

recipes.name: Tofu and egg bibimbap-style rice bowl
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Korean bibimbap, with pan-fried tofu, a fried egg and quick vegetables over rice
recipes.about: Warm brown rice topped with golden tofu and mushrooms, wilted spinach, carrot, cucumber and fried eggs, stirred together with a gochujang and sesame sauce. It is ready in about 19 minutes and brings **protein, iron and folate**, with vitamin C from the vegetables to help absorb the iron.

ingredients.note: any kind, patted dry and cubed
grated, or from a bag of slaw mix
sold as vitamin D mushrooms, sliced

steps: Wash the spinach, mushrooms and cucumber. Pat the tofu dry and cube it, slice the mushrooms and heat half the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu and mushrooms about 4 minutes, turning, until the tofu is golden on a few sides.

While they fry, stir the gochujang, rice vinegar, soy sauce and half the sesame oil with a spoonful of water into a sauce. Grate the carrot (or use bagged slaw mix), cut the cucumber into matchsticks and slice the scallion. Tip the tofu and mushrooms onto a plate.
Add the rest of the oil to the pan, crack in the eggs and wash your hands, then fry about 3 minutes, until the whites and the yolks are completely set.

Meanwhile, microwave the rice in a bowl with a splash of water, covered, about 2 minutes, until steaming hot. Then refrigerate the rest of an opened pouch within 1 hour for use within 1 day. In a second covered bowl, microwave the spinach with a splash of water about 1 minute, until wilted. Squeeze out the water and toss the spinach with a few drops of the remaining sesame oil.

Spoon the rice into a bowl and arrange the tofu, mushrooms, eggs, spinach, carrot and cucumber on top. Drizzle with the sauce and scatter with the sesame seeds and scallion, then stir it all together.
recipes.tip: A spoonful of chopped kimchi on top adds crunch and tang. Plain white mushrooms are fine if you cannot find vitamin D ones; you just lose the vitamin D.

recipes.name: Beef pho-style noodle soup with bok choy and basil
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Vietnamese pho bo, with a quick ginger and star anise broth instead of an all-day stock
recipes.about: A fragrant ginger and star anise broth with thin rice noodles, tender slices of beef, bok choy, carrot and a pile of fresh basil, finished with lime. It is ready in about 19 minutes and brings **iron, zinc and protein**, with vitamin C from the lime to help absorb the iron. The second portion makes tomorrow's lunch.

ingredients.note: sliced paper-thin; ask for thin-sliced beef for stir-fry or hot pot
cut into thin matchsticks, or from a bag of slaw mix

steps: Boil a full kettle while you wash and slice the ginger and slice the onion. Put the broth, ginger, onion, star anise and cinnamon in a pot, add an equal amount of hot water from the kettle, cover and bring to a boil over high heat, then simmer 5 minutes. Pour the rest of the hot water over the rice noodles in a big bowl (boil the kettle again if you need more) and soak about 6 minutes, until tender but not mushy, then drain.
While the broth simmers, wash the bok choy, carrot, basil, scallion and lime. Slice the bok choy, cut the carrot into matchsticks, tear the basil and slice the scallion.
Stir the fish sauce, honey and salt into the broth and fish out the star anise. Add the bok choy and carrot and simmer 1 minute.

Slice the beef last if it is not pre-sliced, then wash your hands, the knife and the board. Slip the beef slices into the simmering broth for about 1 minute, until no pink is left and the meat is cooked through.
Divide the noodles between bowls, ladle over the broth and beef and top with the basil, scallion and a squeeze of lime.

Pack the second bowl with its noodles in a separate shallow container from the broth and refrigerate it within 1 hour. Keep it up to 3 days. To reheat, bring the broth to a rolling boil, pour it over the noodles and make sure everything is steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Buy the beef pre-sliced (hot pot or stir-fry cut). Hoisin and sriracha on the table are very Vietnamese, but use them sparingly: both are salty.

recipes.name: Miso-ginger broiled salmon with bok choy and rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese miso-glazed salmon, with the vegetables broiled on the same tray
recipes.about: Salmon brushed with a savoury-sweet miso, ginger and honey glaze, broiled on one tray with bok choy, then served over brown rice and edamame. It brings **omega-3 and B12**, plus some vitamin D, with calcium and vitamin K from the bok choy, in about 18 minutes. The second portion makes tomorrow's lunch.

ingredients.note: skin-on or skinless fillets, about 2 cm thick

steps: Set an oven rack about 15 cm (6 inches) under the broiler and heat it on high. Line a sheet pan with foil. If the salmon is frozen, thaw it in the fridge, use it within 2 days and never refreeze it.

Wash the bok choy and the ginger well. Whisk the miso, soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, grated ginger and garlic with a spoonful of water, then pour half into a clean small bowl for the plate. Halve the bok choy and toss it in a bowl with the oil and the salt.
Set the salmon on the pan and brush the other half of the glaze over the top, then throw away what is left in the brushing bowl. Wash your hands, the brush and the board after touching the raw fish.

Broil the salmon 4 minutes, then add the bok choy around it, cut side up, and broil 5 to 7 minutes more, until the salmon flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and the bok choy edges are browned. Move the pan down a rack if the glaze darkens too fast.

For the last 4 minutes, microwave the rice and frozen edamame in a covered bowl with a splash of water, stirring once, until steaming hot. Then refrigerate the rest of an opened pouch within 1 hour for use within 1 day.

Serve the salmon and bok choy over the rice and edamame with the clean glaze, the sesame oil, sesame seeds and scallion. Pack the second portion into a shallow container before you sit down and refrigerate it within 1 hour. Keep it up to 2 days, cold or reheated once until steaming, 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Thicker fillets need a minute or two more. Check the middle with a thermometer.

recipes.name: Thai basil chicken with fried egg, red pepper and rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Thai pad kra pao, the street stir-fry, made with chicken breast and plenty of vegetables
recipes.about: Chopped chicken stir-fried hot and fast with garlic, chili, sweet red pepper, carrot, mushrooms and a big handful of basil, topped with a fried egg and served over brown rice with edamame. It is done in about 19 minutes and gives you **lean protein, choline and vitamin A**. The second portion makes tomorrow's lunch.

ingredients.note: from a bag of slaw mix, or cut into thin matchsticks
sold as vitamin D mushrooms, sliced

steps: Wash the pepper, carrot, mushrooms, basil and lime. Slice the chicken into thin strips (cutlets are fastest), then chop it into small pieces. Wash your hands, the knife and the board straight away.

Slice the pepper and mushrooms and mince the garlic. Use slaw mix for the carrot, or cut it into matchsticks. Squeeze the lime. Stir the soy sauce, fish sauce, honey and salt together in a small bowl.

Heat two-thirds of the oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Add the chicken and stir-fry about 3 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink is left and the largest piece reaches 74 °C (165 °F). Meanwhile, microwave the rice and frozen edamame in a covered bowl with a splash of water until steaming hot, then refrigerate the rest of an opened pouch within 1 hour for use within 1 day.

Add the garlic, chili flakes, mushrooms, pepper and carrot and stir-fry about 3 minutes, until the vegetables are crisp-tender. At the same time, heat the rest of the oil in a small non-stick pan, crack in the eggs and wash your hands, then fry about 3 minutes, until the whites and yolks are completely set.
Pour the sauce into the wok and toss 1 minute, then take it off the heat and stir in the basil and lime juice.

Serve the chicken over the rice and edamame with an egg on each portion. Pack the second portion, egg and all, into a shallow container before you sit down. Refrigerate it within 1 hour. Keep it up to 3 days and reheat it once, until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Lower the chili flakes for a mild version. Fresh Thai chilies are the classic if you like it hot. Plain white mushrooms are fine if you cannot find vitamin D ones.

recipes.name: Thai green curry with shrimp and vegetables
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Thai gaeng keow wan, made with a store-bought curry paste and lighter coconut milk
recipes.about: Plump shrimp, sweet red pepper, bok choy and spinach in a creamy, fragrant green curry, served over brown rice. A good paste does the work of a dozen ingredients, so it is on the table in about 18 minutes with **protein, iodine and vitamin C**. The second portion makes tomorrow's lunch.

ingredients.note: peeled and deveined, thawed in the fridge if frozen
check the label: many pastes contain shrimp paste or fish
a few handfuls, from a bag

steps: Wash the pepper, bok choy, spinach, basil and lime. Slice the pepper and bok choy and squeeze the lime. If the shrimp is frozen, thaw it overnight in the fridge, use it within 2 days and never refreeze it. Pat it dry and wash your hands after touching it.
Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add the curry paste and fry about 1 minute, stirring, until it smells fragrant.
Stir in the coconut milk and the broth, bring to a simmer, then add the pepper and bok choy and simmer 4 minutes, until they are just tender.
Add the shrimp and cook about 3 minutes, until they are pink, opaque and curled. Stir in the spinach, fish sauce and salt until the spinach wilts, about 1 minute.

Meanwhile, microwave the rice in a covered bowl with a splash of water until steaming hot, then refrigerate the rest of an opened pouch within 1 hour for use within 1 day. Take the curry off the heat and stir in the lime juice and basil.

Spoon the curry over the rice. Pack the second portion into a shallow container before you sit down and refrigerate it within 1 hour. Keep it up to 3 days and reheat it once, until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Pastes differ a lot in heat and salt. Start with less, taste, and add more. For a shellfish-free curry, use a paste with no shrimp and swap the shrimp for chicken.

recipes.name: Broiled mackerel with sesame soba, cucumber and egg
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese saba shioyaki and cold soba, with a soy and rice vinegar dressing
recipes.about: Atlantic mackerel fillets broiled until crisp, over cool buckwheat soba tossed with cucumber, slaw, edamame and a sesame-ginger dressing, with a halved boiled egg on top. It brings **omega-3 and B12** in about 18 minutes. The second portion makes tomorrow's lunch.

ingredients.note: Atlantic mackerel fillets, not king mackerel
boiled until the yolk is firm
from a bag of slaw mix, or finely shredded
from the slaw mix, or grated

steps: Buy the mackerel very fresh or frozen and keep it cold, and thaw frozen fillets in the fridge. Cook it within 2 days. Do not cook it if it smells off, and stop eating if a bite tastes peppery or makes your mouth tingle. Set an oven rack about 12 cm (5 inches) under the broiler and heat it on high. Line a sheet pan with foil. Fill a large pot with water from the kettle and bring it to a boil. Gently lower the eggs into the boiling water and set a timer for 10 minutes.

Wash the cucumber, ginger and scallion and rinse the slaw unless the bag says it is ready to eat. Slice the cucumber and scallion, then stir the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, honey, grated ginger and salt together to make the dressing.

Pat the mackerel dry, lay it skin side up on the pan. Spoon a little of the dressing into a separate small bowl, brush it over the fish, then throw away what is left in that bowl. Wash your hands and the board after touching the raw fish and the raw eggs.
Broil 6 to 8 minutes, until the skin is blistered and the flesh flakes and reaches 70 °C (158 °F).

When the eggs have had about 5 minutes, add the soba to the same pot for about 4 minutes, adding the frozen edamame for the last 2 minutes. Lift out the eggs when the timer rings and cool them under cold water. Drain the soba and edamame, rinse under cold water and shake dry.

Peel and halve the eggs. Toss the soba and edamame with the cucumber, slaw, scallion, sesame seeds and the rest of the dressing and top with the mackerel and eggs. Cool the second portion within 1 hour, keep it in a shallow container in the fridge up to 2 days, and eat the noodles cold and the fish cold or reheated once to 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Hard-boiled eggs from the fridge skip the egg timer. Skip the cold rinse if you want the soba warm, but cool the leftovers quickly. Tonight, microwave a rice pouch until steaming, spread it on a plate, cool it and refrigerate it within 1 hour for tomorrow night's fried rice (about 3 minutes).

recipes.name: Kimchi egg fried rice with tofu and spinach
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Korean kimchi bokkeumbap, made with cold, day-old rice
recipes.about: Cold rice fried hot with tangy kimchi, golden tofu, mushrooms, edamame and a firm scramble of eggs, finished with sesame oil and a handful of spinach. Cold rice fries up fluffy and separate, and the dish brings **protein, choline and folate** in about 19 minutes.

ingredients.note: cold, from a pouch heated and chilled the night before, or leftover rice
any kind, patted dry and cubed
chopped, with a splash of its juice
sold as vitamin D mushrooms, sliced

steps: The night before, microwave the rice pouch in a covered bowl until steaming hot, spread the rice on a plate or tray, cool it, cover it and put it in the fridge within 1 hour. Use it the next day. Cold, dry rice is what makes fried rice fluffy.
Wash the spinach, mushrooms and scallion. Pat the tofu dry and cube it, slice the mushrooms and chop the kimchi. Mince the garlic and slice the scallion.

Beat the eggs and wash your hands and the board after cracking them. Heat half the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Pour in the egg and scramble about 1 minute, until completely set and firm. Tip it onto a plate.
Add the rest of the oil, the tofu and the mushrooms and fry about 3 minutes, turning, until the tofu is golden on a few sides. Add the garlic, kimchi and frozen edamame and fry 1 minute.

Add the cold rice, breaking up any clumps, and stir-fry 3 to 4 minutes, until it is steaming hot all the way through, 74 °C (165 °F). Stir in the soy sauce, the spinach and the egg and toss until the spinach wilts.
Finish with the sesame oil, sesame seeds and scallion. Eat it right away. Fried rice has used its one reheat, so do not save the leftovers.
recipes.tip: Heat and chill the rice the night before; Friday's mackerel recipe reminds you. Plain white mushrooms are fine if you cannot find vitamin D ones.

recipes.name: Miso soba soup with tofu, egg and spinach
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese miso soup and hot soba, made into a fast noodle supper
recipes.about: A savoury miso broth with buckwheat soba, firm tofu, egg ribbons, edamame, mushrooms and spinach, finished with scallion and a grind of pepper. The tofu and egg make it **a high-protein bowl**, ready in about 17 minutes.

ingredients.note: sold as vitamin D mushrooms, sliced

steps: Wash the spinach, mushrooms, ginger and scallion. Beat the egg in a small bowl, then wash your hands. Slice the mushrooms and scallion, thinly slice the ginger and cube the tofu.
Bring the broth and an equal amount of water to a simmer in a pot with the ginger, mushrooms and frozen edamame and cook 3 minutes.
Add the soba and the tofu and simmer about 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until the noodles are tender.

Turn the heat to low. Drizzle in the beaten egg in a thin stream, stirring gently, and cook about 2 minutes, until the egg is completely set and firm. Stir in the spinach and let it wilt, about 30 seconds. Put the miso in a ladle, stir in a little broth to loosen it and stir it back into the pot. Do not boil the soup after the miso goes in.
Ladle into a bowl and top with the scallion and a grind of black pepper.
recipes.tip: Dried wakame in tiny amounts is welcome in miso soup, but keep it small because seaweed is very high in iodine. Plain white mushrooms are fine if you cannot find vitamin D ones.

recipes.name: Ginger-garlic chicken with bok choy and mushrooms over rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese home-style chicken and greens stir-fries
recipes.about: Thin slices of chicken stir-fried with ginger, garlic, mushrooms and bok choy in a light soy and rice vinegar sauce, spooned over brown rice. It takes about 18 minutes and brings **lean protein, vitamin C and vitamin K**, with the sauce soaked up by the rice.

ingredients.note: sold as vitamin D mushrooms, sliced

steps: Wash the bok choy, mushrooms, ginger and scallion. Slice the chicken into thin strips, then wash your hands, the knife and the board. Slice the mushrooms, cut the bok choy into pieces, slice the ginger and garlic and slice the scallion.
Stir the soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey and broth together in a small bowl.
Heat the canola oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Add the chicken and stir-fry about 3 minutes, until no pink is left and the largest piece reaches 74 °C (165 °F). Lift it onto a plate.
Add the ginger, garlic and mushrooms to the pan and stir-fry about 2 minutes, until the mushrooms soften. Add the bok choy and stir-fry about 2 minutes, until the stems are crisp-tender.

Return the chicken, pour in the sauce and toss about 1 minute, until it bubbles and coats everything. Meanwhile, microwave the rice in a covered bowl with a splash of water until steaming hot, then refrigerate the rest of an opened pouch within 1 hour for use within 1 day.
Spoon over the rice and finish with the sesame oil and scallion.
recipes.tip: Plain white mushrooms are fine if you cannot find vitamin D ones; you just lose the vitamin D.

recipes.name: Warm edamame with chili and lime
recipes.about: Steaming edamame tossed with lime, a pinch of salt and chili flakes, the bar snack of Japan. It is a quick hit of **plant protein and fibre**.
steps: Put the frozen edamame in a bowl with a splash of water, cover and microwave about 3 minutes, until steaming hot.
Wash the lime, then drain the edamame, toss with the lime juice, chili flakes and salt, and eat while warm.

recipes.name: Tangerine and walnuts
recipes.about: Sweet, juicy tangerine segments with a handful of walnuts. The walnuts bring **omega-3 and vitamin E**, plus a satisfying crunch.
steps: Wash the tangerine, then peel it and pull it into segments.
Eat with the walnuts.

recipes.name: Smashed cucumber with sesame and rice vinegar
recipes.about: Cucumber smashed so it soaks up a garlicky soy and rice vinegar dressing, then showered with sesame seeds. It is cool, crunchy and light, with a little **sesame for copper and vitamin E**.
steps: Wash the cucumber. Smash it with the flat of a knife or a rolling pin until it cracks, then tear or cut it into bite-size pieces.
Toss with the rice vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil and garlic, and scatter the sesame seeds on top.
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese pai huang gua, smashed cucumber salad

recipes.name: Carrot sticks with miso-walnut yogurt dip
recipes.about: Crunchy carrot sticks with a creamy dip of Greek yogurt, a little miso, finely chopped walnuts and lime. The carrots bring **vitamin A and fibre**, and the yogurt adds protein and calcium.
steps: Wash the carrots and the lime. Cut the carrots into sticks and juice the lime.
Stir the yogurt, miso, walnuts and lime juice together until smooth.
Serve the carrot sticks with the dip.

recipes.name: Cold tofu with ginger, soy and scallion
recipes.about: Cool, smooth cubes of firm tofu with a little grated ginger, soy sauce and sesame oil, the Japanese hiyayakko. It is a **protein-packed snack** in 5 minutes.
steps: Wash the scallion and ginger. Drain the tofu, pat it dry and cut it into cubes or slabs.
Top with the ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil and scallion. Keep opened tofu covered in water in the fridge and use it within 3 days.

recipes.name: Warm soy milk with toasted sesame and honey
recipes.about: A mug of warm calcium-fortified soy milk with a spoonful of toasted sesame seeds and a drizzle of honey, in the spirit of Chinese black sesame drinks. It brings **calcium and protein**, with sesame for copper and vitamin E.
steps: Shake the carton, pour the soy milk into a mug and heat it in the microwave about 1 minute, until steaming.
Stir in the honey and scatter the sesame seeds over the top.
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese black sesame soy milk

recipes.name: Warm soy milk with walnuts
recipes.about: A mug of warm calcium-fortified soy milk with a handful of walnuts, a simple comfort snack in China and Taiwan. It brings **calcium, protein and a little omega-3**.
steps: Shake the carton, pour the soy milk into a mug and heat it in the microwave about 1 minute, until steaming.
Sip it with the walnuts.
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese warm soy milk
